```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`biosyntax` highlights biological text without parsing or changing the data.
It returns ANSI, HTML, or semantic spans and accepts several Bioconductor
classes.

# Text input

```{r}
library(biosyntax)

vcf_lines <- c(
  "##fileformat=VCFv4.3",
  "#CHROM\tPOS\tID\tREF\tALT\tQUAL\tFILTER\tINFO",
  "chr1\t42\t.\tA\tG\t60\tPASS\tDP=12"
)

x <- biosyntax(vcf_lines, format = "vcf")
biosyntax_spans(x)
x
```

# Biostrings

```{r, eval=requireNamespace("Biostrings", quietly=TRUE)}
dna <- Biostrings::DNAStringSet(c(ref = "ACGTACGT", alt = "ACGTNCGT"))
biosyntax(dna)
```

DNA and RNA use the nucleotide color scheme. Amino-acid sequences use the
CLUSTAL scheme by default.

# VariantAnnotation

```{r, eval=requireNamespace("VariantAnnotation", quietly=TRUE)}
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".vcf")
writeLines(c(
  "##fileformat=VCFv4.2",
  "##contig=<ID=chr1,length=1000>",
  "#CHROM\tPOS\tID\tREF\tALT\tQUAL\tFILTER\tINFO",
  "chr1\t42\t.\tA\tG\t60\tPASS\t."
), path)
vcf <- VariantAnnotation::readVcf(path, genome = "example")
biosyntax(vcf)
unlink(path)
```

# GenomicRanges

```{r, eval=requireNamespace("GenomicRanges", quietly=TRUE) && requireNamespace("rtracklayer", quietly=TRUE)}
gr <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("chr1:10-20")
biosyntax(gr, format = "bed")
```

# Explicit output

```{r}
ansi <- as_ansi(x)
html <- as_html(x)
```
